# Hook method

**How much do we engineer the opening lines?** · [all approaches](index.md) · clashes: C17, C34


## Triple hook: context, lean, snapback
<a id="triple-hook"></a>

The topic is said, shown and written in the first words. The second line gives a reason to keep watching. The third line pulls the viewer the opposite way.

**Looks like:** Frame 1: the object is on screen, the topic is in big text, and the same words are spoken. Line 2 adds a number or a pain ('...and it's why your shoulders aren't growing'). Line 3 flips it ('The fix isn't lighter weight.'), with a punch-in and a thud. The body then pays off the flip.

**Good at:** low skip rate; instant clarity; repeatable recipe; works in any niche

**Weak at:** can feel formulaic if every reel uses it; needs a written script

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches all · goals retention, reach · effort medium

**How:** Write the three lines before filming. In Edits/CapCut, put the context text on frame 1 under the spoken line and add a punch-in plus a hit on the snapback.

**Backed by:** [Triple hook: context, lean, snapback](../topics/hooks.md#hook-triple-hook-formula), [Context in the first words, three channels](../topics/hooks.md#hook-context-first-words), [Lean: proof, pain/benefit or shock](../topics/hooks.md#hook-lean-three-ways), [Untangle: hook, format, topic, illustration](../topics/growth.md#growth-untangle-data), [Desire hook: this is exactly what you want to see](../topics/hooks.md#l11-desire-hook) · sources L01

## Say something crazy and get into it
<a id="say-something-crazy"></a>

No hook formula. Open with the boldest honest line you have and start the content at once.

**Looks like:** The first second is a blunt line straight to camera with no setup text ('I'd never buy a gaming laptop again'). There's no title card and no context line. The reasons start on the next breath, and the energy carries it.

**Good at:** speed to make; natural energy; feels unscripted; good for confident talkers

**Weak at:** hit or miss; context can arrive late and raise skips; hard to repeat on purpose

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short, story · niches all · goals speed, comments · effort low

**How:** Record three or four different openers in one take and keep the strongest. Only trims and captions in Edits.

**Backed by:** [Don't overthink: say something crazy](../topics/hooks.md#hook-say-something-crazy), [Teaching format: template card, then a real example](../topics/editing.md#l11-template-then-example), [Hook template bank (fill in the blanks)](../topics/hooks.md#l11-hook-template-bank), [B&W freeze for sarcastic punchlines](../topics/effects.md#fx-bw-freeze-punchline), [Re-record the intro at the end](../topics/filming.md#film-redo-intro-at-end) · sources L08

## Statement, reason, re-hook, 'Why?'
<a id="statement-reason-rehook"></a>

Briar's live build: a strong statement, a one-sentence reason, a stronger re-hook with higher stakes, then 'Why?' to open the next loop.

**Looks like:** 'Most PC shops overcharge beginners.' (statement) 'They know you won't check the RAM speed.' (reason) 'And I've seen it cost people ₹15,000.' (re-hook) 'Why?' The answer runs through the middle of the reel, and a new loop opens at about 15 s.

**Good at:** holds viewers past 15 s; stacked curiosity; fits talking-head reels

**Weak at:** needs a real stake to escalate; long hooks can drag in short reels

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long · niches all · goals retention, comments · effort medium

**How:** Write four short lines. Edit the 'Why?' as its own beat (a hard cut or a text pop) so it reads as a turn.

**Backed by:** [Statement, reason, re-hook, "Why?", payoff](../topics/story.md#story-live-hook-build), [Open loops, re-open one at ~15 s](../topics/story.md#story-open-loops), [Don't overthink: say something crazy](../topics/hooks.md#hook-say-something-crazy), ["8 Mile": disprove the counter-argument first](../topics/story.md#story-8-mile) · sources L08, L05

## Three hooks at once: title, verbal, visual
<a id="title-verbal-visual"></a>

Design the text hook, the spoken hook and the visual hook as three separate pieces that land together.

**Looks like:** The top text says one thing ('8 GB GPU = ₹50,000 wasted'). The spoken line says a related thing ('Shops still push this card'). The visual is an action (the GPU box slammed on the desk, or a retention graph). Each channel adds something instead of repeating.

**Good at:** thumb stop; works with sound off; proof in the first 2 s

**Weak at:** three things to design and sync; can overload the first frame

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short, carousel · niches all · goals reach, retention · effort medium

**How:** Plan the three hooks in the script. Build the title in CapCut/Edits text, or as a HyperFrames title card, timed to the visual action.

**Backed by:** [Hook = title + verbal + visual](../topics/hooks.md#hook-title-verbal-visual), [Claim plus instant visual proof](../topics/hooks.md#hook-bold-claim-visual-proof), [Untangle: hook, format, topic, illustration](../topics/growth.md#growth-untangle-data), [Teaching format: template card, then a real example](../topics/editing.md#l11-template-then-example), [Hook template bank (fill in the blanks)](../topics/hooks.md#l11-hook-template-bank) · sources L07, L01, L03

## Cold open on later highlights
<a id="cold-open-montage"></a>

A long video opens on a fast montage of its best later moments before the start.

**Looks like:** The first 30–50 s are the most extreme lines and shots from later in the video, cut fast with music. Then a title, and the slower main body begins. Viewers know the payoff exists before they commit.

**Good at:** long-form retention; sets expectations; doubles as a trailer clip

**Weak at:** spoils some payoffs; too long for short form

**Best for:** formats yt-long, podcast · niches all · goals retention · effort medium

**How:** After the main edit, pull 5–8 peak moments and cut them on beats in CapCut, or as an ffmpeg concat with a music bed.

**Backed by:** [Cold open with later highlights](../topics/hooks.md#hook-cold-open-montage), [Hook window: 2–3 s short, 15–20 s long](../topics/hooks.md#hook-window-short-vs-long), [Context in the first words, three channels](../topics/hooks.md#hook-context-first-words), [Re-record the intro at the end](../topics/filming.md#film-redo-intro-at-end) · sources L08, L09, L05

## Proven template, fill the blanks
<a id="template-bank"></a>

Keep a bank of hook templates with blanks ([X], [Y], [niche]) taken from reels that went viral, each with its proof; pick one and fill it for your idea.

**Looks like:** Before scripting, Srijan fills three templates for the same idea ('Never build a PC if…', '10 saal ka PC pain in 60 seconds', 'This is exactly what you wanna see…'), keeps the strongest and rewrites the words in his own Hinglish with his real numbers.

**Good at:** speed; never a blank page; proven structures; easy to A/B several openers

**Weak at:** anyone can use the same line (C34); formulaic if every reel uses it; proof of the template is someone else's views

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, carousel · niches all · goals speed, retention, reach · effort low

**How:** Swipe file (template | example link | views | niche) in the Brain or Notes. Fill 3 per idea, then run L09's tests (visualise, falsify, nobody else) on the winner.

**Backed by:** [Hook template bank (fill in the blanks)](../topics/hooks.md#l11-hook-template-bank), [Challenge, ranking and list templates](../topics/hooks.md#l11-classic-hook-templates), [Teaching format: template card, then a real example](../topics/editing.md#l11-template-then-example), [Lead-magnet CTA over a recap strip](../topics/growth.md#l11-lead-magnet-recap-cta) · sources L11

## Mixing
Triple hook and the three-channel stack combine naturally (the context line is the title). Briar's statement-reason-rehook is a triple hook that keeps going. A cold open can end on a triple hook. A filled template can be the context-lean of a triple hook; Srijan's own numbers and self-roast are what make it 'nobody else could say it'.

## Rule of thumb
Short teaching or proof reels: triple hook or the three-channel stack. Raw yaps or volume weeks: say something crazy. 60 s and up: statement-reason-rehook. Long form: cold open. Blank page or a busy week: template bank, then rewrite in your voice.
